title: The Kuroshio Loop Current in the winters of 2014-2017
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: Three-Dimensional Structure and Interannual Variability of the Kuroshio Loop Current in the Northeastern South China Sea

period_match.paper_data: ten moorings west of the Luzon Strait, satellite altimetry
period_match.supplied_data: CMOMS model velocity, temperature and salinity
period_match.note: The paper also ranks events in the 1993-2019 altimeter record, which lies partly outside the supplied record (finding 4).

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: The Kuroshio Loop Current occurs mainly in winter.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The 3-yr moored data between 2014 and 2017 revealed that the KLC mainly occurred in winter'.
criteria.how_to_test: A loop-current index (for example the anticyclonic circulation or dynamic-height anomaly southwest of Taiwan, about 118-121 E, 19.5-22.5 N) by month for 2011-2020.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: peak season exact)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: Near the Luzon Strait the loop current is confined to the upper 500 m; farther into the South China Sea it becomes more barotropic.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'initially confined to the upper 500 m near the Luzon Strait, but it became more barotropic, with kinetic energy transferring from the baroclinic mode to the barotropic mode when it extended into the SCS interior'.
criteria.how_to_test: Vertical structure of the velocity anomaly along the loop from the strait into the interior; the barotropic share of kinetic energy by location (the mooring sections were along about 119.9 E and 21 N).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: velocity e-folding depth near the strait +/-150 m; sign of the along-path change in barotropic share exact)

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: A loop-current identification adapted from the paper's mooring velocities and altimeter SSH to model fields; the winter season; a modal decomposition or another justified barotropic and baroclinic split.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: Model versus moored observations; a forced model need not reproduce the timing of individual eddy-shedding events; the 1993-2019 altimeter context lies outside the record; no winds.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
